rules.concern: A valid signature establishes attestation, not authority.

Authorization additionally requires a valid non-revoked key, recognized issuer, valid authority derivation and lineage, signer authorization power, scope coverage, and temporal/state predicates that hold.
Commitments use RFC8785 canonical bytes with a registered ASCII domain, NUL separator, and SHA-256.
Commitment text is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters with no prefix or surrounding whitespace.
Registered domain strings contain only ASCII bytes 0x21..0x7E, contain no NUL byte, and are version-specific.
Artifact domains come only from the closed protocol registry and unknown domains fail closed.
Verifier derives expected domain from artifact type; artifact-supplied domain cannot choose the commitment domain.
Implementations must not dynamically construct security domains from artifact_type; only closed registered mappings are valid.
Signature input is reconstructed from the closed-schema unsigned envelope and the signature member is excluded from signed bytes.
Ed25519 signatures and future public keys use strict unpadded RFC4648 base64url with decode/reencode canonicality and exact decoded lengths.
Signed artifact type and signed artifact domain must match the closed registry.
Signature text permits only the unpadded URL-safe base64 alphabet; padding, whitespace, alternate alphabets, noncanonical encodings, and wrong decoded lengths fail closed.
The Ed25519 signature input is exactly ASCII(PROOFRAIL:SIGNATURE:V1) followed by one NUL byte followed by UTF8(JCS(E_tau)), where E_tau is the unsigned closed-schema signature envelope.

Raw security artifacts pass resource limits, strict UTF-8, tokenization, duplicate-name detection, lexical profile, I-JSON, schema, semantic validation, canonicalization, commitment, signature, key, authority, and protocol validation in order.
Duplicate property names are detected before map/object conversion and escaped names compare after escape processing.
BOM, comments, trailing commas, NaN, infinities, invalid UTF-8, lone surrogates, multiple top-level values, unsupported JSON extensions, and leading/trailing whitespace are rejected.
The admitted wire value is exactly one top-level JSON object; non-object top-level JSON values are rejected before canonicalization or commitment.
Canonicalization performs no Unicode normalization, folding, transliteration, or homoglyph replacement.
Property ordering follows RFC8785 UTF-16 code-unit ordering and invalid Unicode fails closed.
Security-critical JSON numeric tokens are nonnegative decimal integers in 0..2^53-1 with no sign, decimal, exponent, or forbidden leading zero.
Numeric restrictions are enforced against original lexical tokens before host-language numeric conversion and recursively in extensions.

Signed values, larger integers, decimal-precision quantities, money, timestamps, hashes, cryptographic quantities, and arbitrary-precision values use strings with explicitly registered grammars rather than unrestricted JSON numbers.
Signed timestamps use exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, UTC only, uppercase T/Z, fixed widths, no fractional seconds, no whitespace, valid calendar values, and no leap second 60.
Wall-clock timestamps do not implicitly establish transaction ordering; deterministic ordering uses logical epoch or another explicitly committed logical sequence.

logical_epoch, issued_at, observed_at, received_at, expires_at, and evidence_deadline are distinct roles; wall-clock values establish temporal validity only under an explicitly committed clock policy.
Every signed security-relevant artifact carries the mandatory protocol header and empty extension containers in ESRM v0.1.
Unknown critical extensions fail deterministically and security meaning cannot enter through uncommitted extension material.
Implementations must not reorder arrays unless the protocol schema explicitly defines sorted-set construction before artifact construction.

All extension material inside a governed artifact is included in canonical bytes and the domain-separated commitment; retained noncritical metadata must have explicitly defined lack of security effect.
Reconciliation result algebra is exactly MATCH, DIVERGED, INSUFFICIENT, and UNRESOLVED with mutually exclusive meanings.
Timeout does not imply divergence; open-window uncertainty is INSUFFICIENT and closed-window unresolved uncertainty is UNRESOLVED.
Later evidence creates a new reconciliation artifact or epoch rather than mutating an earlier conclusion.
A reconciliation conclusion belongs to the ADJUDICATED domain and is not itself empirical evidence.
Absence of observed evidence is not evidence of absence unless authoritative closed-world coverage over the relevant domain and interval is proven and committed.
Evidence establishing authoritative closed-world coverage is itself retained and cryptographically committed.
Authority consumption is append-only and irreversible; later proof of rejection, non-effect, crash, or timeout cannot restore the consumed authority.
A legitimate later attempt after consumption requires a distinct newly derived authority; proof of non-occurrence may justify regrant but never reuse.
RESERVATION_CANCELLED and AUTHORITY_CONSUMED are distinct; a reservation may be cancelled only before consumption.
Consumed authority, consumed transition identifiers, and consumed nonces must never be accepted for reuse.

Authority consumption is not equivalent to external effect; AUTHORITY_CONSUMED must be durably recorded before CROSSING_POSSIBLE, and both records precede any externally visible effect-capable dispatch.
After CROSSING_POSSIBLE without conclusive external evidence, effect status is UNKNOWN and cannot be converted to success, failure, or reusable authority.
The dispatch lifecycle distinguishes UNDISPATCHED, DISPATCH_INTENT_RECORDED, AUTHORITY_CONSUMED, CROSSING_POSSIBLE, DISPATCH_ACKNOWLEDGED, EFFECT_CONFIRMED, EFFECT_REJECTED, and EFFECT_UNRESOLVED.
A crash after durable consumption/crossing but before transmission may burn authority without effect; this availability loss must not be repaired by silently restoring authority.
Dispatch intent is an immutable, domain-committed artifact establishing prepared authorized attempt only, not transmission, execution, observation, or settlement.

Dispatch-intent artifacts carry the Section 35 frozen fields including transition_id, transition commitment, authority-consumption commitment, executor identity, target, operation, effect identity, dispatch sequence, logical epoch, and mandatory header/extensions, and are committed under PROOFRAIL:DISPATCH-INTENT:V1.
Boundary-crossing artifact proves only that the protected effect boundary could be crossed; it does not prove transport or effect.

Immediately before dispatch a durable boundary-crossing artifact carries the Section 36 frozen commitments and identities linking transition, intent, consumption, attempt, effect, target, and logical epoch with mandatory header/extensions.
Target recovery capability cannot be established by adapter self-declaration; it requires committed capability evidence.
Durable idempotency evidence must establish same effect identity plus same canonical payload implies at most one semantic effect.
Target capability class is one of ATOMIC_PARTICIPANT, DURABLE_IDEMPOTENCY, CONDITIONAL_MUTATION, QUERYABLE_EFFECT, OBSERVABLE_ONLY, or OPAQUE_TARGET.
Recovery relies on committed target-capability evidence that existed for the transition, not capability claims introduced after a crash.
For QUERYABLE_EFFECT, capability evidence defines whether a negative query proves non-occurrence or only lack of current knowledge.
For OBSERVABLE_ONLY and OPAQUE_TARGET, ambiguous dispatch forbids automatic retry.
Recovery observes occurred effects, starts a new transition after proven non-occurrence, retransmits the same effect only with verified durable idempotency, otherwise remains unresolved.

Retransmission under durable idempotency preserves effect identity, canonical operation commitment, target, and semantic transition; any security-relevant change creates a new transition requiring new authority.
Proof of non-occurrence never restores original consumed authority; RECOVER_WITH_NEW_TRANSITION requires a newly derived transition and authority.

Recovery branching is defined only over a valid durable crossing artifact D, valid durable-idempotency evidence K for the exact effect identity, admissible authoritative effect-status evidence Q, and admissible final non-occurrence evidence F; unqualified evidence cannot drive an occurred, non-occurrence, or retransmission branch.
Transport attempts and semantic effects are distinct; multiple attempts belong to one transition only with verified durable deduplication.
Transport acknowledgement and executor response are not independent proof of semantic effect or empirical observation.
Transport-attempt records remain independently distinguishable from transition, observation, reconciliation, and settlement artifacts.
ESRM v0.1 does not claim universal exactly-once execution.
Unknown external effect status never becomes false success, false failure, or restored execution authority.
Cryptographic validity, authority validity, and empirical validity remain distinct; speculative, empirical, and adjudicated epistemic roles remain distinct.
Settlement requires independently distinguishable committed facts for state, derivation, authority, admission, consumption, dispatch, observation, reconciliation, and settlement.

The protocol preserves the byte-level boundary RawBytes->StrictParse->Schema->CanonicalBytes->DomainCommitment->SignatureAttestation->AuthorityValidation and the external execution boundary Intent->Consume->CrossingPossible->Dispatch->Observe->Adjudicate->Settle.
